The Assistant Director of Development for Health & Sciences Development & Alumni Relations is an experienced professional who has the ability to practice, and/or has knowledge of, the fundraising field, with the ability to apply fundraising theory to the full range of responsibilities of a university development officer. This position analyzes problems/issues of varied scope, and determines solutions, and plans, schedules, and implements comprehensive fundraising projects and programs, including fundraising programs such as the Children’s Miracle Network.

This position is metric-driven and expected to raise gift dollar amounts as established through an annual business planning process and aligned with the assigned portfolio. This is a fundraising position focused on developing new and fostering established donor relationships. Guided by a “donor centric” approach, the incumbent will strategically solicit gifts and steward existing ones using various communication methods, including in person, video, texting, phone, social media and virtual visits. jobs.description:
About The Agency

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.

As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.

Your Team

The Office of Development (OOD) leads the agency’s effort to create and preserve affordable housing in collaboration with other HPD offices as well as other city, state and federal agencies. The OOD is comprised of eight divisions that administer a range of programs. These divisions include Portfolio Management & Conversions, New Construction Finance, Special Needs Housing, Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), Homeownership Opportunities and Preservation, Preservation Finance, Compliance and Enforcement, and Housing Incentives.

The Division of Portfolio Management & Conversions (PMC) manages development projects after closing with an initial loan to manage rent restructuring and conversion to permanent financing, to deploy rental assistance to tenants prior to project stabilization, to ensure projects’ adherence to program and accounting requirements, and to facilitate timely completion. As a relatively new division in the OOD, PMC administers multiple programs areas including Conversions & Rental Assistance, Requisitions, and Construction Monitoring & Completions.

Within OOD, PMC collaborates especially closely with the Division of Preservation Finance (PF) on a substantial shared portfolio of projects. As a result, PMC and PF share additional executive and operational support, including an Associate Commissioner and an Executive Director of Policy and Operations, that support both divisions.

Program Areas Within The Division

The Conversions team oversees the conversion of construction loans to permanent financing, a critical checkpoint for HPD to ensure that development teams have adhered to program requirements, and to set up these projects for long-term success for decades to come. The unit also oversees rent restructuring, a process through which HPD resets rents in a project in accordance with various laws, regulations, and program policies, and which is a critical tool to ensure housing affordability and long-term project stability. All of this involves managing due diligence requirements, managing multiple external stakeholders to overcome barriers to achieving these milestones, establishing new rent-stabilized rents, and close coordination with a broad array of HPD staff.

The Rental Assistance team plays a key role in ensuring tenants in HPD-financed affordable housing are able to access rental assistance, and that projects reach rental achievement targets in a timely manner in order to convert to permanent financing. This work includes direct outreach and assistance to tenants, reviewing tenant income certifications for projects that provide preferential rent offers, and close coordination with the Division of Tenant and Owner Resources around the provision of rental assistance to eligible households.

The Requisition unit is responsible for the financial administration, implementation, and close-out of HPD’s construction loan for a portfolio of moderate rehabilitation loan programs within the Division of Preservation Finance, including the Participation Loan, LIHTC Year 15, Multifamily Housing Rehabilitation, and HUD Multifamily Loan Programs. GHPP, MHRP, and HUD Multifamily. This team is responsible for processing construction requisition packages for payment, and processing construction change orders for projects whose construction is monitored by BLDS. Requisitions is the liaison between the loan programs, BLDS, partner lenders, construction loan servicers, HPD Fiscal Affairs, HPD Legal, owners/borrowers, and contractors for these matters throughout the construction period. This unit also tracks progress of and oversees close-out of a portfolio of Preservation Finance projects for which loan servicing and construction monitoring is managed by an external partner.

The Construction Monitoring & Completions team is responsible for monitoring the portfolio of HPD-assisted affordable housing projects during construction to track and report out on construction progress, to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve significant construction and completion issues that could adversely impact project budgets and timelines, and to establish, track, and facilitate achievement of project completion targets. This growing unit coordinates closely with the Division of Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), OOD’s Executive Operations team, and other teams in PMC to support projects’ timely completion, ensure compliance with BLDS and Program policies, and support projects’ efficient deployment of subsidy in support of HPD’s mission.

Your Impact

The Division of Portfolio Management & Conversions seeks an experienced professional with strong leadership, analytical, and management abilities to be the Director of Operations (D of O) responsible for all areas of operation within the division of more than 25 staff across multiple teams.

The D of O reports to the Assistant Commissioner for Portfolio Management and Conversions and plays a key role in developing and supervising division operations and activities, including personnel, data tracking and management, policy, budget, and planning actions for all components of the division.

Your Responsibilities

As Director of Operations, you will direct, coordinate, and conduct operational activities for the Division. You will facilitate personnel and hiring actions for each unit within the division as well as supporting teams and the Assistant Commissioner for data exercises and information requests. You will serve as a liaison to the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and to the Executive Office Chief of Staff. You will also serve as a main point of contact in coordinating activities within and outside of the Division of Portfolio Management and Conversions.

The D of O will directly supervise the Director of Requisitions, Executive Assistant, and other staff as appropriate.

Duties include, but are not limited to, the following main areas:

Data and Tracking:
Coordinate with division teams, Executive Director of Policy and Operations, and the Executive Director of PMC on key data and tracking exercises, and assist in responding to incoming requests from outside of the division
Provide strategy, tracking, and oversight for operations areas such as requisition and change order approval, violations monitoring, project close-out and handoff, completions targeting, rental assistance allocation, fiscal/budget, technology needs, workspace coordination, and personnel matters
As needed, analyze and create reports on the completion and conversion outputs of the Division in a manner that facilitates decision making, strategizing, and capital project budget forecasting
In conjunction with the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and D of O for Preservation Finance, ensure tracking and compliance on key divisional priorities and reporting/document retention obligations
Hiring and Personnel:
In coordination with the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and Executive Director for PMC, coordinate hiring, onboarding, and offboarding for teams within the division, including but not limited to setting up job interviews, drafting and submitting hiring paperwork, liaising with HPD’s Budget and Human Resources teams, and serving on interview panels as needed
Drive recruitment and hiring initiatives to efficient completion, optimizing onboarding timelines in partnership with division supervisors and HPD’s Budget and HR teams
Provide oversight and strategic guidance to supervisors, including participation in meetings with staff as needed, on personnel matters and performance appraisal processes
Coordination and Communication:
Assist divisional- and office-wide efforts to assess and update policy and procedures that are in line with the goals of the entire Division; under the guidance of the Assistant Commissioner, you will play an integral role in developing policy regarding programmatic and personnel matters within the Division. This could include but may not be limited to coordinating with other divisions, research, developing proposals, meetings with elected officials, and brainstorming new program needs.
Serve as a liaison to the Directors of Operation for Preservation Finance and for BLDS to ensure expeditious approvals of requisitions and change orders, minimize delays in completion and close-out, and allocate rental assistance resources strategically across the PF and PMC portfolios.
With support from the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and Executive Director for PMC, assess the training needs of the entire division, coordinate participation in training and other opportunities
Disseminate information from the various areas of the agency to the Division. Information could include but not be limited to: new data entry rules, policy initiatives, and current events related to housing
Coordinate with the Administrative Operations staff for divisional meeting and calendar management, event preparation, and other functions as needed
Advocate for the operational needs of the division in cross-agency conversations, as needed
As needed, represent the Assistant Commissioner and the Division at meetings and be called upon by the Assistant Commissioner to assist in the preparation of materials for internal and external meetings.

The D of O may be assigned other duties, as needed, by the Assistant Commissioner.

Preferred Skills

Strong analytical, research, organizational, and quantitative skills; demonstrated experience in proactive problem solving;
Demonstrated ability to meet deadlines and manage projects in a timely manner;
Ability to perform complex tasks with limited supervision;
Experience in staff management and talent recruitment;
Excellent verbal, written communication, and presentation skills; excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in collaboration with others and in the supervision of others;
Strong follow-through and focus on timely results;
Experience working for or with government agencies or government programs related to affordable housing development is a plus;
Familiarity with financial modeling and business process analysis is a plus;
Strong facility with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint required.

Please note, finalists for this position must have filed for the Open Competitive Associate Housing Development Specialist exam #4122 or promotional exam #4570. In addition, the position is open to applicants who are already permanent in the Associate Housing Development Specialist title, or permanent in another comparable civil service title. Candidates must indicate permanent civil service title on resume.

ASSOCIATE HOUSING DEVELOPMENT - 22508

Minimum Qualifications

A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and three years of full-time satisfactory professional experience in the development, appraisal, financing, negotiation, or disposition of real estate, or in real estate law, or in urban planning or analytical or coordination work related to housing programs; or
A four year high school diploma or its educational equivalent approved by a State's Department of Education or a recognized accrediting organization and seven years of full-time satisfactory experience as described in "1" above

jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Director of Communications and Systems is a senior leadership role responsible for building and maintaining MHET's brand, communications infrastructure, digital systems, and organizational operations. This role drives how MHET tells its story – to funders, community members, partners, and the public – while also ensuring the internal systems that power the organization run smoothly and effectively. The Director oversees communications strategy, content creation, graphic design, social media, PR, the website, email marketing, HubSpot, and Asana, and manages the Operations & HR Manager and two part-time staff. This is a high-output, high-ownership role for someone who is equally comfortable building a workflow, writing a press release, designing a flyer, and managing a team. 

About MHET

Mid-Hudson Energy Transition, Inc. (MHET)
is a not-for-profit community-based organization that empowers communities to own and share renewable energy, create healthier buildings, and join in community wealth-building to strengthen the resilience of the Hudson Valley in the face of climate change. We engage and build on the active involvement of communities, with particular emphasis on low-income and communities of color that are being harmed first and worst by climate change.

Responsibilities

Communications Strategy & Content (35%)

Develop and execute MHET's overall communications strategy across all channels and audiences – community members, funders, partners, media, and the public.
Write and edit a wide range of content including newsletters, blog posts, press releases, grant narratives, impact reports, talking points, and program materials; ensure all communications are clear, compelling, and aligned with MHET's voice and values.
Manage MHET's monthly newsletter, including list management, segmentation, content curation, design, and performance analysis. Support the publication of MHET’s donor, board, and HELP Fund Investor newsletters in collaboration with program leads.
Lead media and public relations efforts, including building relationships with journalists and media outlets, drafting press releases, pitching stories, and positioning MHET as a recognized voice in the energy justice space.
Develop, edit, or outsource thought leadership content – including blogs, panels, reports, and media appearances – in collaboration with program and leadership staff to amplify MHET's model and expertise regionally and nationally.
Develop and maintain internal communications tools for staff, including program-specific talking points, scripts, and FAQs, so that all team members can represent MHET's work clearly and consistently in the field.
Ensure compliance with HELP and HELP Fund marketing and advertising guidelines across all program-related materials.
Own and maintain MHET's crisis communications plan; lead scenario planning and staff training to ensure organizational preparedness.
Ensure all communications materials are culturally responsive, accessible, and reflective of the communities MHET serves.

Digital Presence & Design (25%)

Manage and maintain MHET's website, keeping content current, accurate, and strategically organized; update the impact page and program pages on a regular cadence.
Lead MHET's social media presence across platforms – developing content calendars, creating and scheduling posts, monitoring engagement, and growing audience.
Design graphics, flyers, event pages, program materials, presentations, and other visual assets using tools such as Canva; maintain brand consistency across all materials.
Create and manage event pages, online forms, and digital campaigns to support program recruitment, fundraising, and community engagement using tools such as Google Ads, Givebutter, Rippling, and use data to improve strategy over time with tools such as Google Analytics.
Track and report on digital performance metrics – including social media KPIs, website traffic, email open and click rates, and form submissions – and use data to improve strategy over time.

Systems & Operations (30%)

Own and continuously improve MHET's HubSpot CRM – building and maintaining pipelines, workflows, automations, forms, and reporting dashboards for communication efforts, programs, development, and outreach.
Oversee MHET's Asana infrastructure, ensuring project boards, templates, and team workflows are organized, up to date, and used consistently across the organization.
Serve as the connective tissue across programs – ensuring HUG, HELP, EI, and Outreach are operating from shared systems, consistent data, and aligned communications infrastructure.
Supervise the Operations & HR Manager, serving as their primary point of contact and accountability for day-to-day administrative functions including payroll, accounts payable and receivable, vendor management, record retention, and compliance documentation.
Oversee IT infrastructure and technology needs in coordination with the Operations & HR Manager, ensuring staff have the tools and access they need; manage vendor relationships for software, hardware, and tech services.
Support the Operations & HR Manager in executing HR processes including onboarding, offboarding, benefits administration, and employee record-keeping; escalate sensitive HR matters to the Executive Director.
Ensure financial and administrative processes are well-documented and consistently followed; flag issues or exceptions to the Executive Director as appropriate.
Identify and implement tools, process improvements, and integrations that increase organizational efficiency and effectiveness across all departments.

Impact Reporting & Funder Communications (10%)

Lead the development and publication of MHET's annual impact report and program-specific impact materials, synthesizing data from across programs into compelling, accessible narratives for funders, partners, and the public.
Build and maintain reporting systems and templates that enable program staff to consistently capture outcomes, participant stories, and key metrics throughout the year.
Support grant reporting in collaboration with the Executive Director and program staff, ensuring deliverables are accurate, on time, and tell a strong story.
Collaborate with program directors to collect and elevate participant testimonials, case studies, and qualitative impact data that center lived experience in all reporting.
Support the Executive Director and Managing Director on funder communications, sponsorship stewardship, and donor-facing materials.
Plan and execute fundraising and community events, managing logistics, marketing, sponsorship fulfillment, volunteer coordination, and follow-up.

Qualifications

Studies have shown that women and people of color may be less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every one of the qualifications listed. We are most interested in finding the best candidate for the job. We would encourage you to apply for this position even if you don’t meet every one of our qualifications listed.

Required:

5+ years of experience in communications, marketing, or a related field, preferably in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated ability to create high-quality written content across a range of formats and audiences – from community-facing program materials to funder-facing grant narratives.
Experience managing social media accounts and digital marketing campaigns, with a track record of growing engagement and reach.
Proficiency in graphic design tools (e.g., Canva) and ability to produce polished, on-brand visual materials independently.
Experience building or managing CRM systems, preferably HubSpot, including workflow automation, pipeline management, and reporting.
Strong project management skills, including experience with tools such as Asana and the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously.
Experience planning and executing events, including logistics, marketing, and stakeholder coordination.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail; able to manage a high volume of work without sacrificing quality.
Deep commitment to environmental justice, equity, and community-centered work.
Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills; able to work across teams and support staff communications needs.

Desirable:

Experience with website management and content updates (WordPress or similar).
Experience with fundraising, development, or grant writing in a nonprofit context.
Knowledge of New York State energy policy, clean energy programs, or environmental justice landscape.
Bilingual English/Spanish.
Familiarity with the Hudson Valley region and its communities.
LEED, ESG, or sustainability-related credentials.

Location, Schedule and Availability

Mid-Hudson Energy Transition is located in Kingston, NY. The daily work schedule is Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm. This is a hybrid position, with a strong preference for candidates who are able to work on-site several days per week and flexibility to work remotely the remainder of the time. 

Compensation and Benefits

The salary for this position is $90,000 and generous benefits, including 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance; retirement plans with a 4% employer match; professional development opportunities; and unlimited paid time off.

To Apply

Please submit your resume and references to our Careers Page . We will review applications on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. We appreciate all applications, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Executive Director

THRIVE Center for Survivors of Torture

POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director (ED) holds overall strategic and operational responsibility for THRIVE’s staff, programs, finances, and execution of its mission. The ED serves as THRIVE’s chief executive and principal public representative, leads a senior team of Clinical, and Medical Directors, and partners closely with the Board on governance, strategy, and fundraising.
The ED is expected to hold this work with the seriousness it deserves: THRIVE’s clients are survivors of severe trauma, and the organization’s effectiveness depends on services that are clinically sound, culturally responsive, and delivered by a team that is well supported.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Executive Director’s responsibilities fall into six areas.
1. Board Partnership & Strategic Leadership

•      Serve as the Board’s primary staff partner: prepare meeting materials, support committee work, and provide the timely, accurate information on mission, finances, program outcomes, and risk that the Board needs to govern well.
•      Develop, maintain, and support a strong Board of Directors, including partnering on recruitment, orientation, and ongoing development of board members.
•      Ensure THRIVE has a long-range strategy that advances its mission, and that the organization makes consistent and timely progress toward it.
•      Develop organizational and financial plans with the Board and carry out the plans and policies it authorizes.
•      Ensure THRIVE carries out its mission with integrity and in conformity with the highest ethical standards in all respects.
•      Use data to inform decisions about clients, programs, and staffing, and build the organization’s capacity to do so.
•      Maintain official records and documents and ensure the organization’s continuity through documented systems and succession planning.
2. Fundraising & Development

•      Plan and implement THRIVE’s annual and long-term fundraising strategy, with an emphasis on revenue diversification and reducing concentration risk.
•      Prepare or oversee all funding applications and proposals for federal, state, county, city, foundation, corporate, and individual support.
•      Research and cultivate new donor relationships, with particular attention to major gifts.
•      Steward existing funders through accurate reporting, site visits, renewals, and consistent relationship management.
•      Grow individual giving, including the annual appeal and any donor events or campaigns.
•      Engage and support the Board in its fundraising role, including introductions, cultivation, and solicitation.
3. Financial Management, Compliance & Administration

•      Prepare the annual organizational budget for Board approval, along with program and grant budgets.
•      Ensure that adequate funds and cash flow are available for THRIVE to carry out its work, managing restricted and unrestricted funds and building operating reserves.
•      Hold overall responsibility for finances and accounting, and ensure the accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of all financial reporting.
•      Oversee the monthly close in partnership with the contracted accounting firm, using Dext and QuickBooks; ensure expenses are allocated to the appropriate funding sources and that reports for contract reimbursement and Board review are produced on schedule.
•      Review and submit financial reports and requests for reimbursement, manage accounting and audit vendors.
•      Prepare all documentation required for the annual audit and Form 990, and review both with the Board of Directors.
•      Serve as approver for payables in Bill.com within Board-approved authority limits, maintaining clear separation between the preparation and the approval of payments.
•      Work with the bookkeeper and Board Treasurer to maintain strong internal controls, appropriate segregation of duties, and sound financial practices.
•      Execute contracts with grantors, contractors, and other partners, and ensure obligations under them are met.
•      Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, including federal award requirements: allowable costs and cost principles under the Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), time-and-effort documentation, subrecipient and vendor monitoring, single audit readiness, and timely programmatic and financial reporting to ORR and other federal, state, and local funders.
•      Maintain the organization’s insurance coverage, registrations, and risk management practices.
4. Program Oversight & Quality

•      Collaborate with THRIVE’s Clinical and Medical Directors, and Program Manager to design, deliver, and improve programs, and to assess staff and organizational effectiveness.
•      Ensure services remain trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically accessible, including adequate interpretation capacity.
•      Oversee outcome measurement and evaluation, ensuring the organization tracks what matters to clients and funders and uses the results to improve services.
•      Ensure compliance with clinical, privacy, and confidentiality requirements, including HIPAA, licensure and credentialing, and mandatory reporting obligations.
•      Ensure programs are appropriately staffed and resourced relative to caseload and client acuity, and that referral and intake processes function well.
•      Maintain a working knowledge of significant developments and trends in the field of torture rehabilitation, and in the immigration and refugee policy environment affecting THRIVE’s clients.
5. Internal Leadership, People & Culture

•      Recruit, supervise, develop, and evaluate the senior leadership team; develop or adapt job descriptions as needed.
•      Manage the human resources of the organization according to authorized personnel policies and procedures that fully conform to current laws and regulations.
•      Maintain a workplace culture that is communicative, cooperative, and resourceful, and in which staff can raise concerns and expect to be heard.
•      Sustain practices that protect a clinical team doing trauma work from vicarious trauma and burnout, including adequate clinical supervision, manageable caseloads, meaningful use of paid time off, and modeling those norms as a leader.
•      Oversee staff professional development and support staff in reaching their professional goals.
•      Review compensation and benefits periodically for competitiveness and internal equity, and recommend adjustments to the Board.
6. External Relations & Community Partnership

•      Serve as THRIVE’s chief spokesperson, representing the organization to agencies, funders, partner organizations, and the general public.
•      Establish sound working relationships and cooperative arrangements with other nonprofit organizations, government agencies, health systems, and the national consortium of torture treatment programs.
•      Oversee new and existing external partnerships, delegating relationship management within the organization where appropriate.
•      Oversee communications and public presence, website, email, social media, and print, to publicize THRIVE’s activities, programs, and goals.
•      Advocate, within the limits appropriate to a 501(c)(3) organization, for policies and resources that serve survivors of torture.
•      Protect client privacy and dignity in all external communication and storytelling.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The salary range for this position is $100,000 to $115,000 annually, commensurate with experience.
We provide a comprehensive benefits package, including:
•        80% employer-paid health, dental, vision, and life insurance. 25% employer paid dependent coverage
•        401k with a 3% match, eligible from the start date.
•        Flexible work schedule.
•        Paid lunchtime, holidays, vacation, sick leave, and self-care time.
•        Generous training and professional development opportunities.
•        A trauma-responsive culture that prioritizes self-care, professional development, and a client-centered approach to healing.

HOW TO APPLY

Applications will be received until Friday September 25, 2026.

jobs.title: Associate Director of Development, Peabody
jobs.description:
Peabody College of Education and Human Development at Vanderbilt University seeks an experienced and highly motivated development professional to serve as Associate Director of Development. Reporting to the Senior Director of Development for Peabody College, the Associate Director will serve as a front-line fundraiser responsible for cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major gift donors and prospects in support of the College’s highest priorities.

The Associate Director will manage a portfolio of alumni, parents, friends, and other prospective donors with the capacity to make gifts generally ranging from $25,000 to $250,000. The position will develop and execute thoughtful, individualized strategies to build meaningful relationships with donors and connect their philanthropic interests with opportunities to advance Peabody College’s mission and priorities.

Fundraising responsibilities will encompass a broad range of priorities, including student financial aid and scholarships, faculty support, and strategic programs and initiatives across Peabody College. These may include but aren’t limited to Roberts Academy & Dyslexia Center, Next Steps, Programs for Talented Youth, Susan Gray School, and other emerging priorities.

The Associate Director will work closely with the Peabody team (4), Dean Camilla Benbow, and senior leadership of Peabody College, faculty, program and center leaders, alumni, volunteers, and colleagues across Vanderbilt’s Development and Alumni Relations organization. The successful candidate will bring strong relationship-building skills, sound fundraising judgment, excellent communication abilities, and a demonstrated commitment to advancing the mission of higher education.

About The Work Unit

The Department of Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) assists Vanderbilt University in securing the resources, both human and financial, that are required to achieve its mission and goals. The Department is responsible for the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of individuals and organizations whose charitable objectives are consistent with those of Vanderbilt University’s teaching and research programs. Learn more about our department at https://www.vanderbilt.edu/dar/

Key Functions And Expected Performance

Major Gift Fundraising and Portfolio Management

Manage a portfolio of major gift prospects and donors, developing and executing individualized strategies for identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with alumni, parents, friends, foundations, and other prospective donors.
Personally solicit and close major gifts, generally in the range of $25,000 to $250,000, in collaboration with the Senior Director and other university and college leaders as appropriate.
Develop and maintain an active prospect pipeline, identifying opportunities to move prospective donors toward deeper engagement and philanthropic investment.
Establish annual fundraising goals and activity plans in partnership with the Senior Director and contribute meaningfully to Peabody College’s overall fundraising objectives.
Conduct donor visits and participate in meetings, events, and other engagement opportunities designed to cultivate and steward donors and prospects.
Ensure timely and appropriate stewardship of major gift donors, demonstrating the impact of their philanthropy and strengthening long-term relationships.

Peabody College Priorities

Raise philanthropic support for Peabody College’s strategic priorities, with particular emphasis on:- Student financial aid and scholarships;
Faculty support, including professorships, faculty development, and other opportunities to recruit and retain outstanding faculty;
The Roberts Academy & Dyslexia Center;
Next Steps;
Programs for Talented Youth;
Susan Gray School; and
Other academic programs, centers, institutes, and strategic initiatives as assigned.
Develop a strong understanding of Peabody College’s academic programs, research, faculty expertise, and distinctive centers and initiatives in order to articulate compelling philanthropic opportunities to donors.
Translate donor interests and passions into meaningful opportunities for investment that advance Peabody College’s strategic priorities.
Partner with academic and program leaders to develop compelling cases for support, donor engagement opportunities, proposals, and stewardship materials.

Collaboration and Relationship Management

Partner closely with the Senior Director of Development to develop and implement comprehensive fundraising strategies for assigned prospects and priorities.
Work collaboratively with the Dean, senior college leadership, faculty, program and center directors, and other key stakeholders to advance fundraising priorities.
Coordinate with colleagues across Vanderbilt Development and Alumni Relations, including development officers, annual giving, principal gifts, foundation relations, corporate relations, gift planning, advancement communications, prospect development, and stewardship.
Collaborate with university and college colleagues to ensure coordinated and strategic engagement of donors and prospects.
Serve as a knowledgeable and trusted development partner to Peabody College faculty and staff, providing guidance on donor engagement and fundraising strategy.

Fundraising Communications and Proposals

Prepare and coordinate compelling proposals, letters, briefing materials, impact reports, and other written materials to support donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Develop individualized proposals and solicitation strategies that align donor interests with Peabody College priorities.
Assist in developing cases for support and fundraising materials for strategic initiatives, programs, and centers.
Prepare senior leaders and faculty for donor meetings, solicitations, and stewardship engagements.

Events and Donor Engagement

Participate in and help plan events and engagement opportunities designed to cultivate, solicit, and steward major gift donors and prospects.
Leverage Peabody College events, faculty interactions, student experiences, and program activities to deepen donor engagement and strengthen relationships.
Represent Peabody College and Vanderbilt University with professionalism and enthusiasm in interactions with donors, alumni, parents, volunteers, and external partners.

Advancement Operations and Reporting

Maintain accurate and timely records of donor interactions, strategies, proposals, solicitations, and other activity in Vanderbilt’s advancement systems.
Prepare prospect plans, contact reports, solicitation documentation, and other required advancement records.
Monitor portfolio activity and fundraising progress and provide regular updates to the Senior Director of Development.
Participate in team meetings, professional development activities, and strategic planning efforts.

Other Responsibilities

Perform other duties and special projects as assigned in support of Peabody College’s fundraising and advancement priorities.

Supervisory Relationships

This position has no supervisory responsibility; this position reports administratively and functionally to the Associate Dean Development, Peabody & Executive Director of Strategic Initiatives.

Work Environment

Hybrid role based in Nashville – in the office approximately 1 day per week depending on business needs.

Education And Certifications

Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience And Skills

Required Qualifications

At least four years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising, development, sales, relationship management, or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain productive relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds.
Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, organizational, and project management skills.
Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively to a collaborative development team.
Willingness and ability to travel and participate in occasional evening and weekend events.
Commitment to the mission of Vanderbilt University and Peabody College and to the transformative impact of education and human development.
Driving is considered an essential job function for this role. Must have and maintain a valid driver's license and a satisfactory driving record. Vanderbilt University engages a third party to provide up-to-date notifications regarding negative changes to motor vehicle records.

Preferred Qualifications

Four or more years of successful experience in major gift fundraising, preferably in higher education or another complex nonprofit environment.
Demonstrated success cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding gifts of $25,000 or more.
Experience managing a portfolio of major gift donors and prospects.
Experience working with academic leaders, faculty, volunteers, and senior institutional leadership.
Experience fundraising for scholarships, financial aid, faculty support, academic programs, centers, or other strategic initiatives.
Familiarity with the principles and practices of comprehensive fundraising campaigns.
Knowledge of Vanderbilt University, Peabody College, or the higher education landscape is preferred but not required.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Demonstrated understanding of major gift fundraising principles and practices.
Exceptional relationship-building and interpersonal skills.
Strong ability to listen, identify donor interests, and align those interests with institutional priorities.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex academic and programmatic priorities in compelling and accessible ways.
Strong strategic thinking, judgment, initiative, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and relationships while meeting deadlines and fundraising goals.
Ability to collaborate effectively with senior leaders, faculty, volunteers, donors, and colleagues across a complex organization.
High level of professionalism, discretion, integrity, and commitment to ethical fundraising practices.
Proficiency with standard office technology and advancement databases.

Position Impact

The Associate Director of Development will play an important role in advancing the philanthropic priorities of Peabody College and Vanderbilt University. Through meaningful relationships with donors and prospects, the Associate Director will help secure resources that expand access to a Peabody education, strengthen the College’s faculty, and advance innovative programs that improve the lives of children, students, families, and communities.

This position offers an opportunity for a talented development professional to work within one of the nation’s leading colleges of education and human development and to make a tangible impact through philanthropy in areas ranging from financial aid and faculty support to nationally recognized programs serving individuals with dyslexia, neurodiverse learners, talented youth, and young children.

About The Agency

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.

As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.

Your Team

The Office of Development (OOD) leads the agency’s effort to create and preserve affordable housing in collaboration with other HPD offices as well as other city, state and federal agencies. The OOD is comprised of eight divisions that administer a range of programs. These divisions include Portfolio Management & Conversions, New Construction Finance, Special Needs Housing, Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), Homeownership Opportunities and Preservation, Preservation Finance, Compliance and Enforcement, and Housing Incentives.

The Division of Portfolio Management & Conversions (PMC) manages development projects after closing with an initial loan to manage rent restructuring and conversion to permanent financing, to deploy rental assistance to tenants prior to project stabilization, to ensure projects’ adherence to program and accounting requirements, and to facilitate timely completion. As a relatively new division in the OOD, PMC administers multiple programs areas including Conversions & Rental Assistance, Requisitions, and Construction Monitoring & Completions.

Within OOD, PMC collaborates especially closely with the Division of Preservation Finance (PF) on a substantial shared portfolio of projects. As a result, PMC and PF share additional executive and operational support, including an Associate Commissioner and an Executive Director of Policy and Operations, that support both divisions.

Program Areas Within The Division

The Conversions team oversees the conversion of construction loans to permanent financing, a critical checkpoint for HPD to ensure that development teams have adhered to program requirements, and to set up these projects for long-term success for decades to come. The unit also oversees rent restructuring, a process through which HPD resets rents in a project in accordance with various laws, regulations, and program policies, and which is a critical tool to ensure housing affordability and long-term project stability. All of this involves managing due diligence requirements, managing multiple external stakeholders to overcome barriers to achieving these milestones, establishing new rent-stabilized rents, and close coordination with a broad array of HPD staff.

The Rental Assistance team plays a key role in ensuring tenants in HPD-financed affordable housing are able to access rental assistance, and that projects reach rental achievement targets in a timely manner in order to convert to permanent financing. This work includes direct outreach and assistance to tenants, reviewing tenant income certifications for projects that provide preferential rent offers, and close coordination with the Division of Tenant and Owner Resources around the provision of rental assistance to eligible households.

The Requisition unit is responsible for the financial administration, implementation, and close-out of HPD’s construction loan for a portfolio of moderate rehabilitation loan programs within the Division of Preservation Finance, including the Participation Loan, LIHTC Year 15, Multifamily Housing Rehabilitation, and HUD Multifamily Loan Programs. GHPP, MHRP, and HUD Multifamily. This team is responsible for processing construction requisition packages for payment, and processing construction change orders for projects whose construction is monitored by BLDS. Requisitions is the liaison between the loan programs, BLDS, partner lenders, construction loan servicers, HPD Fiscal Affairs, HPD Legal, owners/borrowers, and contractors for these matters throughout the construction period. This unit also tracks progress of and oversees close-out of a portfolio of Preservation Finance projects for which loan servicing and construction monitoring is managed by an external partner.

The Construction Monitoring & Completions team is responsible for monitoring the portfolio of HPD-assisted affordable housing projects during construction to track and report out on construction progress, to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve significant construction and completion issues that could adversely impact project budgets and timelines, and to establish, track, and facilitate achievement of project completion targets. This growing unit coordinates closely with the Division of Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), OOD’s Executive Operations team, and other teams in PMC to support projects’ timely completion, ensure compliance with BLDS and Program policies, and support projects’ efficient deployment of subsidy in support of HPD’s mission.

Your Impact

The Division of Portfolio Management & Conversions seeks an experienced professional with strong leadership, analytical, and management abilities to be the Director of Operations (D of O) responsible for all areas of operation within the division of more than 25 staff across multiple teams.

The D of O reports to the Assistant Commissioner for Portfolio Management and Conversions and plays a key role in developing and supervising division operations and activities, including personnel, data tracking and management, policy, budget, and planning actions for all components of the division.

Your Responsibilities

As Director of Operations, you will direct, coordinate, and conduct operational activities for the Division. You will facilitate personnel and hiring actions for each unit within the division as well as supporting teams and the Assistant Commissioner for data exercises and information requests. You will serve as a liaison to the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and to the Executive Office Chief of Staff. You will also serve as a main point of contact in coordinating activities within and outside of the Division of Portfolio Management and Conversions.

The D of O will directly supervise the Director of Requisitions, Executive Assistant, and other staff as appropriate.

Duties include, but are not limited to, the following main areas:

Data and Tracking:
Coordinate with division teams, Executive Director of Policy and Operations, and the Executive Director of PMC on key data and tracking exercises, and assist in responding to incoming requests from outside of the division
Provide strategy, tracking, and oversight for operations areas such as requisition and change order approval, violations monitoring, project close-out and handoff, completions targeting, rental assistance allocation, fiscal/budget, technology needs, workspace coordination, and personnel matters
As needed, analyze and create reports on the completion and conversion outputs of the Division in a manner that facilitates decision making, strategizing, and capital project budget forecasting
In conjunction with the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and D of O for Preservation Finance, ensure tracking and compliance on key divisional priorities and reporting/document retention obligations
Hiring and Personnel:
In coordination with the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and Executive Director for PMC, coordinate hiring, onboarding, and offboarding for teams within the division, including but not limited to setting up job interviews, drafting and submitting hiring paperwork, liaising with HPD’s Budget and Human Resources teams, and serving on interview panels as needed
Drive recruitment and hiring initiatives to efficient completion, optimizing onboarding timelines in partnership with division supervisors and HPD’s Budget and HR teams
Provide oversight and strategic guidance to supervisors, including participation in meetings with staff as needed, on personnel matters and performance appraisal processes
Coordination and Communication:
Assist divisional- and office-wide efforts to assess and update policy and procedures that are in line with the goals of the entire Division; under the guidance of the Assistant Commissioner, you will play an integral role in developing policy regarding programmatic and personnel matters within the Division. This could include but may not be limited to coordinating with other divisions, research, developing proposals, meetings with elected officials, and brainstorming new program needs.
Serve as a liaison to the Directors of Operation for Preservation Finance and for BLDS to ensure expeditious approvals of requisitions and change orders, minimize delays in completion and close-out, and allocate rental assistance resources strategically across the PF and PMC portfolios.
With support from the Executive Director of Policy and Operations and Executive Director for PMC, assess the training needs of the entire division, coordinate participation in training and other opportunities
Disseminate information from the various areas of the agency to the Division. Information could include but not be limited to: new data entry rules, policy initiatives, and current events related to housing
Coordinate with the Administrative Operations staff for divisional meeting and calendar management, event preparation, and other functions as needed
Advocate for the operational needs of the division in cross-agency conversations, as needed
As needed, represent the Assistant Commissioner and the Division at meetings and be called upon by the Assistant Commissioner to assist in the preparation of materials for internal and external meetings.

The D of O may be assigned other duties, as needed, by the Assistant Commissioner.

Preferred Skills

Strong analytical, research, organizational, and quantitative skills; demonstrated experience in proactive problem solving;
Demonstrated ability to meet deadlines and manage projects in a timely manner;
Ability to perform complex tasks with limited supervision;
Experience in staff management and talent recruitment;
Excellent verbal, written communication, and presentation skills; excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in collaboration with others and in the supervision of others;
Strong follow-through and focus on timely results;
Experience working for or with government agencies or government programs related to affordable housing development is a plus;
Familiarity with financial modeling and business process analysis is a plus;
Strong facility with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint required.

Please note, finalists for this position must have filed for the Open Competitive Associate Housing Development Specialist exam #4122 or promotional exam #4570. In addition, the position is open to applicants who are already permanent in the Associate Housing Development Specialist title, or permanent in another comparable civil service title. Candidates must indicate permanent civil service title on resume.

A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and three years of full-time satisfactory professional experience in the development, appraisal, financing, negotiation, or disposition of real estate, or in real estate law, or in urban planning or analytical or coordination work related to housing programs; or

The Director of Communications and Systems is a senior leadership role responsible for building and maintaining MHET's brand, communications infrastructure, digital systems, and organizational operations. Mid-Hudson Energy Transition, Inc. (MHET)
is a not-for-profit community-based organization that empowers communities to own and share renewable energy, create healthier buildings, and join in community wealth-building to strengthen the resilience of the Hudson Valley in the face of climate change. We engage and build on the active involvement of communities, with particular emphasis on low-income and communities of color that are being harmed first and worst by climate change.

Communications Strategy & Content (35%)

Develop and execute MHET's overall communications strategy across all channels and audiences – community members, funders, partners, media, and the public.
Write and edit a wide range of content including newsletters, blog posts, press releases, grant narratives, impact reports, talking points, and program materials; ensure all communications are clear, compelling, and aligned with MHET's voice and values.

Develop and maintain internal communications tools for staff, including program-specific talking points, scripts, and FAQs, so that all team members can represent MHET's work clearly and consistently in the field.
Ensure compliance with HELP and HELP Fund marketing and advertising guidelines across all program-related materials.
Own and maintain MHET's crisis communications plan; lead scenario planning and staff training to ensure organizational preparedness.
Ensure all communications materials are culturally responsive, accessible, and reflective of the communities MHET serves.

Digital Presence & Design (25%)

Lead MHET's social media presence across platforms – developing content calendars, creating and scheduling posts, monitoring engagement, and growing audience.

Track and report on digital performance metrics – including social media KPIs, website traffic, email open and click rates, and form submissions – and use data to improve strategy over time.

Systems & Operations (30%)

Oversee MHET's Asana infrastructure, ensuring project boards, templates, and team workflows are organized, up to date, and used consistently across the organization.
Serve as the connective tissue across programs – ensuring HUG, HELP, EI, and Outreach are operating from shared systems, consistent data, and aligned communications infrastructure.
Supervise the Operations & HR Manager, serving as their primary point of contact and accountability for day-to-day administrative functions including payroll, accounts payable and receivable, vendor management, record retention, and compliance documentation.

Identify and implement tools, process improvements, and integrations that increase organizational efficiency and effectiveness across all departments.

Impact Reporting & Funder Communications (10%)

Executive Director

THRIVE Center for Survivors of Torture

POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director (ED) holds overall strategic and operational responsibility for THRIVE’s staff, programs, finances, and execution of its mission. The ED serves as THRIVE’s chief executive and principal public representative, leads a senior team of Clinical, and Medical Directors, and partners closely with the Board on governance, strategy, and fundraising.
The ED is expected to hold this work with the seriousness it deserves: THRIVE’s clients are survivors of severe trauma, and the organization’s effectiveness depends on services that are clinically sound, culturally responsive, and delivered by a team that is well supported.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Executive Director’s responsibilities fall into six areas.
1. Board Partnership & Strategic Leadership

•      Serve as the Board’s primary staff partner: prepare meeting materials, support committee work, and provide the timely, accurate information on mission, finances, program outcomes, and risk that the Board needs to govern well.
•      Develop, maintain, and support a strong Board of Directors, including partnering on recruitment, orientation, and ongoing development of board members.
•      Ensure THRIVE has a long-range strategy that advances its mission, and that the organization makes consistent and timely progress toward it.
•      Develop organizational and financial plans with the Board and carry out the plans and policies it authorizes.
•      Ensure THRIVE carries out its mission with integrity and in conformity with the highest ethical standards in all respects.
•      Use data to inform decisions about clients, programs, and staffing, and build the organization’s capacity to do so.
•      Maintain official records and documents and ensure the organization’s continuity through documented systems and succession planning.
2. Fundraising & Development

•      Plan and implement THRIVE’s annual and long-term fundraising strategy, with an emphasis on revenue diversification and reducing concentration risk.
•      Prepare or oversee all funding applications and proposals for federal, state, county, city, foundation, corporate, and individual support.
•      Research and cultivate new donor relationships, with particular attention to major gifts.
•      Steward existing funders through accurate reporting, site visits, renewals, and consistent relationship management.
•      Grow individual giving, including the annual appeal and any donor events or campaigns.
•      Engage and support the Board in its fundraising role, including introductions, cultivation, and solicitation.
3. Financial Management, Compliance & Administration

•      Prepare the annual organizational budget for Board approval, along with program and grant budgets.
•      Ensure that adequate funds and cash flow are available for THRIVE to carry out its work, managing restricted and unrestricted funds and building operating reserves.
•      Hold overall responsibility for finances and accounting, and ensure the accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of all financial reporting.
•      Oversee the monthly close in partnership with the contracted accounting firm, using Dext and QuickBooks; ensure expenses are allocated to the appropriate funding sources and that reports for contract reimbursement and Board review are produced on schedule.
•      Review and submit financial reports and requests for reimbursement, manage accounting and audit vendors.
•      Prepare all documentation required for the annual audit and Form 990, and review both with the Board of Directors.
•      Serve as approver for payables in Bill.com within Board-approved authority limits, maintaining clear separation between the preparation and the approval of payments.
•      Work with the bookkeeper and Board Treasurer to maintain strong internal controls, appropriate segregation of duties, and sound financial practices.
•      Execute contracts with grantors, contractors, and other partners, and ensure obligations under them are met.
•      Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, including federal award requirements: allowable costs and cost principles under the Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), time-and-effort documentation, subrecipient and vendor monitoring, single audit readiness, and timely programmatic and financial reporting to ORR and other federal, state, and local funders.
•      Maintain the organization’s insurance coverage, registrations, and risk management practices.
4. Program Oversight & Quality

•      Collaborate with THRIVE’s Clinical and Medical Directors, and Program Manager to design, deliver, and improve programs, and to assess staff and organizational effectiveness.
•      Ensure services remain trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically accessible, including adequate interpretation capacity.
•      Oversee outcome measurement and evaluation, ensuring the organization tracks what matters to clients and funders and uses the results to improve services.
•      Ensure compliance with clinical, privacy, and confidentiality requirements, including HIPAA, licensure and credentialing, and mandatory reporting obligations.
•      Ensure programs are appropriately staffed and resourced relative to caseload and client acuity, and that referral and intake processes function well.
•      Maintain a working knowledge of significant developments and trends in the field of torture rehabilitation, and in the immigration and refugee policy environment affecting THRIVE’s clients.
5. Internal Leadership, People & Culture

•      Recruit, supervise, develop, and evaluate the senior leadership team; develop or adapt job descriptions as needed.
•      Manage the human resources of the organization according to authorized personnel policies and procedures that fully conform to current laws and regulations.
•      Maintain a workplace culture that is communicative, cooperative, and resourceful, and in which staff can raise concerns and expect to be heard.
•      Sustain practices that protect a clinical team doing trauma work from vicarious trauma and burnout, including adequate clinical supervision, manageable caseloads, meaningful use of paid time off, and modeling those norms as a leader.
•      Oversee staff professional development and support staff in reaching their professional goals.
•      Review compensation and benefits periodically for competitiveness and internal equity, and recommend adjustments to the Board.
6. External Relations & Community Partnership

•      Serve as THRIVE’s chief spokesperson, representing the organization to agencies, funders, partner organizations, and the general public.
•      Establish sound working relationships and cooperative arrangements with other nonprofit organizations, government agencies, health systems, and the national consortium of torture treatment programs.
•      Oversee new and existing external partnerships, delegating relationship management within the organization where appropriate.
•      Oversee communications and public presence, website, email, social media, and print, to publicize THRIVE’s activities, programs, and goals.
•      Advocate, within the limits appropriate to a 501(c)(3) organization, for policies and resources that serve survivors of torture.
•      Protect client privacy and dignity in all external communication and storytelling.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The salary range for this position is $100,000 to $115,000 annually, commensurate with experience.
We provide a comprehensive benefits package, including:
•        80% employer-paid health, dental, vision, and life insurance. 25% employer paid dependent coverage
•        401k with a 3% match, eligible from the start date.
•        Flexible work schedule.
•        Paid lunchtime, holidays, vacation, sick leave, and self-care time.
•        Generous training and professional development opportunities.
•        A trauma-responsive culture that prioritizes self-care, professional development, and a client-centered approach to healing.

Overview

The Goodwin Group is conducting a confidential retained executive search for a Chief Operating Officer (COO) on behalf of a mission-driven public-sector organization focused on affordable housing, community development, and expanding economic opportunity. The organization welcomes accomplished operating executives from public- and private-sector environments, including real estate and local government, who have led complex, highly regulated operations.

The COO will serve as the organization’s senior operational leader and a trusted partner to the Chief Executive Officer, overseeing core operational functions and translating strategy into disciplined execution. The successful candidate will be a hands-on, action-oriented leader who strengthens accountability, builds sustainable processes, and ensures initiatives are completed. This executive must also bring the executive presence to represent the organization when needed and the adaptability to help lead technology modernization, organizational change, and workforce development.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Operations Leadership & Strategy

Serve as a key strategic advisor to the Chief Executive Officer and Executive Leadership Team.
Lead the timely and efficient execution of the organization's strategic plan and strategic initiatives.
Ensure agency-wide operations remain aligned with strategic goals and organizational priorities.
Drive accountability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the organization.

Operational Performance & Service Delivery

Oversee housing programs, resident services, facilities, procurement, human resources, information technology, and other assigned operational functions.
Enhance service delivery, customer experience, and operational consistency.
Monitor daily operations while improving processes, policies, and organizational effectiveness.
Develop opportunities for innovation and modernization across housing programs and customer service.

Compliance, Risk Management & Governance

Ensure agency operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, funding requirements, and organizational policies.
Oversee audits, inspections, risk assessments, quality control measures, and corrective action plans.
Partner with executive leadership to identify and mitigate enterprise risks.
Strengthen organizational governance, accountability, and regulatory compliance.

Financial & Resource Stewardship

Partner with the CFO to align operational priorities with financial objectives.
Support operational budgeting, grant management, funding initiatives, and resource planning.
Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational assets and public resources.
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency while maximizing organizational value.

Board, Community & External Stakeholder Relations

Assist the Chief Executive Officer in supporting the governing board through reports, recommendations, and strategic initiatives.
Develop strong relationships with residents, community organizations, government agencies, developers, and strategic partners.

Team Leadership & Organizational Development

Build and maintain a high-performing leadership team through recruitment, mentoring, coaching, and professional development.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Develop future leaders through coaching, succession planning, and professional development.
Guide senior leaders in fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and exceptional customer service.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Management, Finance, Urban Planning, Real Estate, or a related field required; Master's degree strongly preferred.
15+ years of progressive executive leadership experience, including significant experience in a Chief Operating Officer, Executive Vice President, Deputy Executive Director, Assistant City Manager, Vice President of Operations, or comparable enterprise leadership role.
Proven success leading complex, multi-functional organizations through operational excellence, strategic planning, organizational transformation, performance improvement, and disciplined execution.
Broad leadership experience across operations, governance, compliance, enterprise risk management, budgeting, and organizational performance.
Demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams, develop executive leaders, and create scalable operating models and accountability systems.
Experience developing KPIs, operational dashboards, and performance reporting to support executive decision-making.
Experience within public housing, affordable housing, community development, real estate, property management, local government, or another highly regulated, mission-driven organization strongly preferred; experience working with federally funded programs is desirable. Deep public housing experience is valuable but is not required for an accomplished operational leader with relevant transferable experience.
Strong executive presence with the ability to effectively engage governing boards, elected officials, executive leadership, community stakeholders, and external partners.
Decisive, collaborative, and hands-on leadership style with the ability to combine respect and sound judgment with urgency, accountability, exceptional communication, and unquestioned integrity.

new_jobs.title: Director of Operations
new_jobs.description:
McCabe Industrial Minerals is looking for a Director of Operations to help lead the next stage of growth across our mining and mineral-processing operations.

This position will work directly with the President and serve as a key operational leader across the company. The immediate focus will include helping design, build and commission new production capacity while also improving and expanding our existing plants to meet growing demand. The role will have significant responsibility for capital projects, plant performance, maintenance, personnel, safety, quality and long-term operational planning.

We’re looking for someone who understands how things work — mechanically, operationally and practically. An engineering background is preferred, and experience in aggregates, mining, mineral processing, manufacturing or heavy industrial operations would be particularly valuable. However, we are open to both an experienced industry professional and a younger engineer or operations leader with the ability and ambition to grow quickly into the position.

The Director of Operations will oversee plant managers and production personnel across multiple facilities, develop and improve preventive maintenance programs, identify opportunities to increase production and efficiency, and help manage construction, equipment installation and plant upgrades. The position will also work closely with vendors, contractors and equipment manufacturers and have responsibility for operational costs, safety programs, quality standards and environmental and regulatory compliance.

This is a hands-on leadership position. We need someone comfortable moving between planning a multimillion-dollar capital project and walking through a plant with an operator to figure out why a piece of equipment isn’t performing the way it should. Strong communication, judgment and problem-solving ability matter as much to us as a specific degree or number of years in the industry.

The position can be based in Tulsa or Oklahoma City
and will require regular travel to company facilities and project sites.

Compensation & Benefits
$95,000–$115,000 annual salary

100% company-paid health and dental insurance

Company vehicle

Profit-sharing program

Performance-based bonus incentives

McCabe Industrial Minerals has been mining, processing and marketing industrial minerals since 1976. We operate multiple production facilities serving customers in roofing, road construction and other industrial markets, and we're investing significantly in expanding our production capabilities for the years ahead.
